body:
Goal: give factory behavior and state one owner, with explicit interfaces for the operator CLI, Discord and remote owner MCP.

This is part of #1251 (single-app-to-monorep). Drafting assumption: establish component boundaries in the existing deployment first, in one repository and one Go module with coordinated releases. Separate processes, multi-host operation and independent version support are follow-up scope. These assumptions are the shaping agent's call following the owner's instruction to proceed.

Preserve observable behavior, owner approvals, permissions, retained ticket/code connections, result receipts, delivery recovery, worktree isolation and immutable team captures. Each extraction must leave the current deployment usable, retire the direct paths it replaces, and include compatibility checks and a recovery route for any state migration. No new providers, user features or remote authority are included.

In scope:
- Keep intake/admission, scheduling, workflow/owner gates, Git workspaces, attempt authority, durable results and publication/recovery in core.
- Define bounded commands and read views for existing consumers; preserve authorization at the core boundary.
- Include operator CLI ownership in this story: argument parsing/presentation use core services; local installation/configuration and service lifecycle operations remain usable when the daemon is stopped.
- Keep the familiar command surface and the CLI coordinated with the core release.
- Include only the necessary ticket-adapter cleanup formerly called A: preserve GitHub and Linear, use qualified ticket identities at shared boundaries, and confine legacy GitHub-shaped conversions behind that boundary where still required.
- Give factory state and adapter-private state explicit logical owners without forcing separate databases or processes in this milestone.
- Consume the execution-library boundary without moving factory policy into it.

Completion:
- Core workflows run with Discord and remote MCP disabled.
- Existing CLI command behavior and stopped-daemon availability remain covered.
- GitHub and Linear discovery, owner replies, managed-story operations and result publication preserve qualified identity and retained connection routing.
- Ticket approval remains separate from GitHub code-delivery authority.
- Attempt-scoped agent MCP and result helpers retain live descriptor/broker authority and receipts; remote owner access does not acquire it.
- Adapter contracts do not require exposing SQL rows or orchestrator internals.
- Scheduling, locks, interrupted-run handling and delivery retries retain their existing behavior; targeted recovery and compatibility checks pass.

Dependencies: the completed core uses the execution-library boundary; Discord and remote MCP extraction consume these core contracts and can then be delivered independently.

Out of scope: standalone ticket service, comprehensive ticket rewrite, removing GitHub as the supported code host, independent CLI versions, a new network API or new commands/features.

Evidence: https://github.com/marioatcloudvane/litefactory/blob/539e9d35748d7a38f1d6001b8b11c2998adefe6c/internal/cli/commands.go , https://github.com/marioatcloudvane/litefactory/blob/41cfc1222a7f2644a59e6d8c4f2ccf0eb0ce4cd1/internal/projectconnection/tickets.go and https://github.com/marioatcloudvane/litefactory/blob/436cb605fa217839e7bab176a3861dc5946dcaf0/internal/turn/doc.go . Existing compatibility bridges may remain when they satisfy the boundary.

Related: https://github.com/marioatcloudvane/litefactory/issues/1251

title: Establish factory core contracts and include the operator CLI
